subject: prediction of observed variables in lavaan

messages.author: 6b99899654ca3960
messages.subject: prediction of observed variables in lavaan
parts:
Hello,
I have carried out a path analysis using the sem function in lavaan, for which I am providing the model below:

m <- '
end1 ~ ex1 + ex2 + ex3
end2 ~ end1 + ex3
end3 ~ ex1 + ex3
end4 ~ end3 + end1 + end2
end5 ~ ex1 + ex2 + end1 + end4 + ex3

#upgrading endogenous variables to latents (in order to carry out the predictions)
                end1 =~ en1
                end2 =~ en2
                end3 =~ en3
        end4    =~ en4
        end5 =~ en5



As you can see, I have 3 exogenous variable and the endogenous variables are very much dependent on these and on the interactions with other endogeneous variables.

After obtaining the model summary, I am trying to use the model to obtain 'predicted' values for all endogenous variables from generated newdata using the lavPredict() function. However, I am getting the following error: lavaan ERROR: missing observed variables in dataset. en1 en2 en3 en4 en5.


Can the lavPredict function generate 'unknown' values for the observed variables based on newdata of exogeneous variables? And if yes can you provide instructions as to what I am not doing correctly?


many thanks for providing us with this excellent tool.


regards,

Mario

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: RE: prediction of observed variables in lavaan
parts:
Mario—

     It appears to me that your syntax makes the new factors equivalent to the observed variables.  That being so, and given that your model is recursive, you could obtain predicted values (“y-hat”) using a regression function like lm.  Either way, you must either (a) have some cases where you have actual values for the dependent variables (en1 – en5), so that you can estimate the regression weights, or (b) fix the regression weights to particular values.  You can’t estimate regression weights when you only have values for X and have no values for y.

--Ed Rigdon

messages.subject: Re: prediction of observed variables in lavaan
parts:
You are using the adjustment because your variables are non-normal.  least squares regression does not presume normality in the variables, but in the residuals.  So it is not clear that anything beyond least squares would be needed.
--Ed Rigdon

On 11/22/2014 09:44 AM, Mario Balzan wrote:
> However, I am getting the
> following error: lavaan ERROR: missing observed variables in dataset.
> en1 en2 en3 en4 en5.

Are those variables in the newdata?

This seems to work:

model <- '
fy1 =~ y1
fy2 =~ y2

y1 ~ x1 + x2 + x3
y2 ~ y1 + x1
'
fit <- sem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy)

newdata <- data.frame(y1=rnorm(10), y2=rnorm(10),
x1=rnorm(10), x2=rnorm(10), x3=rnorm(10))
lavaan:::lavPredict(fit, type="lv", newdata = newdata)

Yves.
